incumbent_behaviour.text: Builders are advised to use the generic Webhook trigger module instead of the native Tally app module, because the native module simplifies the payload in a way that complicates handling it downstream.

evidence.quote: Using the app, you’ll receive the data in a simplified version which is easier to handle within Make.

incumbent_behaviour.text: To redirect a respondent after submission, builders are told to skip the Tally module entirely, use a general webhook module, look up a stored response, and send a separate webhook response.

evidence.quote: you don’t use the tally module to redirect the user. You use a general webhook module, search for the response (saved somewhere) and once you find it, you send a webhook response.

incumbent_behaviour.text: When a form platform returns reference numbers instead of readable text for multiple-choice answers, a builder worked around it by building a manual Excel lookup table to translate the codes before using them in later steps.

evidence.quote: for now i have made a bypass and created an excel with all names of activities and the referrence numbers to match them and generate a name to be used on further steps but would be good to have it done properly and also learn the right way.

incumbent_behaviour.text: No-code builders insert a Code node after the Webhook node specifically to reformat incoming form data so it matches the destination database's structure before writing a record.

evidence.quote: Formats the incoming data to match your Notion database structure.

incumbent_behaviour.text: A builder reported constructing their mapping expression using the webhook's field key/label/value structure directly, extracting a specific field with a get(map(...)) function rather than relying on a simplified app module.

evidence.quote: {{get(map(1.data.fields; "key"; "value"); "question_QRZ8Gp")}}

incumbent_behaviour.text: Most publicly shared form-to-CRM automation templates write every incoming submission straight into the CRM with no validation step at all.

evidence.quote: Most form-to-CRM templates going around push whatever arrives straight into the CRM. No check at all.

sophistication_basis.text: These builders are already constructing multi-node automation chains with explicit mapping functions, conditional validation, and CRM upsert logic rather than being unfamiliar with the concept of automation — their stated problems are implementation-level (field mapping, redirects, trigger behavior), not 'what is a webhook'.

evidence.quote: {{get(map(1.data.fields; "key"; "value"); "question_QRZ8Gp")}}

problems.statement: After a Tally form submits to a webhook, the respondent cannot be reliably redirected or shown a conditional response from the automation tool; the connection appears to be lost once the platform returns its own 'accepted' acknowledgement.

evidence.quote: the automatic response message is (accepted), from then on the connection with make would be lost.
how do you ensure that the user does not lose the connection with make once the form is filled out?

problems.statement: A multi-choice form answer passed through a webhook arrives as a reference/ID number rather than the actual answer text, requiring manual identification and correction before it can be used.

evidence.quote: Webhook to Tally forms returning multi choice answer as reference number and not actual text
looks like you mapped the ID instead of the text.

problems.statement: A specific field type from a form webhook (here, email) can fail to write into the destination tool even though the same payload shows the value present and the extraction/logging confirms it is correctly read.

evidence.quote: Only the **email field** is not showing up in Airtable, even though:
Logging the variable → email **is printed correctly** in logs

problems.statement: When testing a newly built scenario, an instant webhook trigger does not process previously received submissions and instead waits for a new one, which can read as the scenario being stuck or broken.

evidence.quote: the scenario doesn’t seem to process any submissions. Instead, it just hangs in an endless loop without handling any data.

problems.statement: Common form-to-CRM automation patterns write submissions directly into the contact database without checking for typos, blank required fields, or bot spam, so bad records accumulate and must be cleaned up by hand afterward.

evidence.quote: Typos, blank names and bot spam land in your contact database, and somebody cleans it up by hand later.

evidence.quote: Most form-to-CRM templates going around push whatever arrives straight into the CRM. No check at all.

desired_outcomes.text: Wants the webhook to send a conditional response or redirect back to the respondent based on their form answers, rather than only the platform's own generic acknowledgement.

evidence.quote: Is it possible to forward to the tally trigger webhook and make a webhook response depending on their answers? help please, thanks.

desired_outcomes.text: Wants submissions that fail validation to be routed to a place a human can review rather than being silently dropped or silently written into the CRM.

evidence.quote: Submissions that pass get upserted and post a “new lead” message in Slack. Submissions that fail go to a separate Slack channel for a human to glance at, so nothing is silently dropped and nothing unchecked is written to the CRM.

signals.text: Zapier's own integration page frames Tally as a form tool whose job is to feed submissions into CRMs, spreadsheets, or databases and trigger notifications — i.e., Tally-as-automation-trigger is a recognized, catalogued use pattern.

evidence.quote: Tally connects with Zapier to automate form submission workflows. Teams use this integration to route submissions, create records in other apps, and notify stakeholders.
